title: Oratomic raises $300M to build a viable quantum computer that needs only 20K qubits
slides: Can a quantum computer work with just 20,000 qubits?
Most designs need millions to beat classical machines.
Oratomic just raised $300M to prove 20K is enough.
Their new architecture cuts error correction hardware by 90%.
Start testing your hardest optimization problem against their emulator.
thread_text:
1. 20K qubits vs. millions

Oatomic just raised $300M betting their architecture can beat classical machines with 20,000 qubits instead of millions.

2. Error correction slashed by 90%

Their new design cuts the hardware needed for error correction by 90%, making smaller qubit counts viable.

3. Emulator is live now

You can test your hardest optimization problem against their emulator today, before the physical chip exists.

4. Most designs need millions

Standard quantum approaches require millions of qubits to outperform classical computers, but Oratomic challenges that assumption.

5. Ready to benchmark your problem?

Go run your toughest optimization against their emulator. Does your current solution still hold up?
